newsitem.title: LATVIA: BALTICS-IMF SEES ESTONIA'S ECONOMY GROWING FASTEST.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS-IMF SEES ESTONIA'S ECONOMY GROWING FASTEST.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Monday that it expected Estonia to have the fastest growing Baltic economy in 1997.
"We forecast that Estonia's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 4.4 percent this year," Dimitris Demekas, the IMF's resident representative in Latvia, told Reuters.
He added that the fund saw Latvia and Lithuania's economies growing by four percent this year.
But he said that the forecast for Latvia, which was made around three months ago, could be revised upward.
"The Latvian forecast may be a bit on the low side...Latvia's economy has recovered much faster from the 1995 banking crisis than we expected," he said.
"The Latvian economy has really bounced back," he said.
He said that Estonia's economy had the best growth prospects as it has been growing the fatest and there was no indication that the government's pro-reform policies would be threatened.
Estonia's economy grew by around four percent in 1996, Lithuania's by 3.6 percent, and Latvia's by about two percent.
